reading:
Figure Ground has now been judged in four rounds. In main rounds 10 and 11 (6.41, then 5.85) the judges loved the rule itself: a plate led by a fine-line figure drawn from its own data (Status's wiring, To do's due queue with NOW, the kinds tally), with a big Plex Condensed title. They sank it on costume and usability: Chapter and Fig. numbering, numbered tracked-caps tabs, mono-caps buttons, every row title a raw blue underline, a glaring paper-grey 'here', an unlit greeting, ISO dates, a 2437px Home and 14 to 20 small targets.

Tour round 1's refine, Lit Manual, fixed all of that and scored 8.02: the tour's highest mean, in all eight top fours, with 6 promise votes. It won because its fixes were themselves new drawings joined to content:
- To do's lit NOW line runs out of the due-queue figure and across the list itself. Six lenses named it the heat's best idea.
- The kinds chart is the Kind filter.
- Status lights its live wire and reads '3 of 4 answering'.
- The lit glass pool and the tall scanlined radar came back.
- 'Tell Vera what to plan.' was first for style, interaction and the skeptic.

Two siblings add evidence. The graft sibling Live Figures (7.3) showed that a round page-head tube holding one live number is 'the most memorable system' (style). It lost on 14px VT323, an amber To do tube, filler figures, numbered tabs and a lost pool. The Cyanotype mutant (5.02) showed that a hue turn or small caps do nothing.

What still holds Lit Manual back, most-cited first:
1. Plans (the harness shoots the month) has no figure and no phosphor, so the lineage's own rule breaks on a named page (feedback, soul, style, system, skeptic).
2. Kind words are 12px tracked mono caps (six lenses).
3. Home's Fig. 1 is a puzzle with a four-symbol legend. It does not touch its rows and draws the next plan as a pale dot (feedback, interaction, usability, skeptic).
4. Head links read as raw-HTML blue (feedback, style).
5. The full steel 'here' slab and the 'Every kind' block are the heaviest solids on the page (feedback, style, skeptic).
6. Figure-led heads leave dark bands on Chat and Status, and the Settings figure column is empty (feedback, system, interaction, skeptic).
7. The chat's sequence diagram is a thumbnail that misses its lines and adds nothing (system, interaction, usability, skeptic).
8. Status's spend is not a green screen (soul, feedback, skeptic).
9. Smaller faults: '#4' ids are read before the titles, the amber-framed tick looks like a different state, READY looks like a button, and the phone hides the figure behind a summary disclosure.

What would make it win:
- Make the NOW line's lesson the lineage's one written rule on every page where it broke: a figure touches its rows, and NOW is lit where a list crosses it.
- Give every live mark the kit's two-layer light, with one real green screen per page.
- Clear the small faults.
- The graft should give the thin places (Plans, Status's spend, the kinds, the relative dates) a figure made of their own data. It should use devices that speak a manual's grammar and replace what is there, not import another lineage's identity.

This round's dice mutant (Lit Manual, Relit) already tests relighting alone, so neither brief should rely on light alone.

briefs.name: Lit Manual, Revised
briefs.hypothesis:
Lit Manual won heat b (8.02, all eight top fours) because its fixes were drawings joined to content: To do's NOW line leaves its figure and crosses the list. Every remaining fault the eight lenses named sits where that did not happen:
- Plans has no figure.
- Home's figure floats beside its rows behind a legend to learn.
- The chat's diagram misses its lines.
- Status's figures sit in the head and leave dark bands.

This edition writes one rule, 'a figure touches its rows', and makes it hold on every page:
- the rail for every list in time: To do, Home's Coming up, the Plans list;
- a week rail that sends NOW across the month grid;
- lifelines as the thread's own gutter;
- the wiring leading its lamps.

That completes the idea on the pages the judges said broke it. The kit's two-layer light goes on every live mark, and the small usability faults are cleared. The judges read 'the refinement that drew new content' as more than a clean-up, and that is what this is.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-figure-refine's files: palettes/t1-figure-refine.json, variants/t1-figure-refine/sheet.css and its templates.

Keep:
- the plate: a 2px rule on top, the slate drawing sheet #0f161c with its 12/48 grid in the 16.5rem figure column, bone words #dcd8ca on #0b100d at the right, one hairline between;
- one lit mark per figure;
- blueprint (#6f88b3 lines, #9fb4d6 accent) as the one cool companion;
- the Plex Sans Condensed, Plex Sans, Plex Mono and VT323 set;
- the lit greeting pool;
- 0 small targets on every page.

Write the edition's rule in _ui.html's header comment: A FIGURE TOUCHES ITS ROWS. Where a plate lists things in time, its figure is THE RAIL: level with each row, in the figure column, the row's date sits on one blueprint line (1.25px --draw), with a stop at the row's own height and a dotted leader over the hairline into the row. NOW is a lit phosphor rule that leaves the rail and crosses the list where the time falls. Where a plate lists connections, the figure is the wiring. Where it is a conversation, the figure is the lifelines.

SYSTEM (every page)
1. The rail as shared parts.
- Generalise To do's .q-mark, .q-dot, .q-date, .now-rule and .now-line (sheet.css about 1561-1660, tasks.html 83-148) into .rail-mark, .rail-dot, .rail-date and .now-rule.
- Every railed list is a grid spanning the figure column and the words (grid-column 1/-1, subgrid), so each mark is a cell of its own row and cannot miss it. Row heights may vary.

2. Light (phosphor_kit.md).
- --lit-mark becomes two layers: drop-shadow(0 0 2px rgb(109 255 156/.85)) drop-shadow(0 0 10px rgb(109 255 156/.38)).
- .now-line: box-shadow 0 0 3px rgb(109 255 156/.8), 0 0 14px rgb(109 255 156/.32), with its #e4fff0 lamp core.
- The key word 'plan' keeps E1.
- Pointing at or focusing a row lights its own rail dot, stop, arrow or port in 0.12s and lets it go over var(--afterglow), 1.2s. For the rails use plain li:is(:hover,:focus-within) rules. For the SVG figures use the :has() pattern the Settings callouts already use (sheet.css about 1779).
- One green screen per page: Next up on Home, the radar on Ideas, the spend tube on Status. Elsewhere the NOW line and each figure's one live mark are the light.
- The screen and the glows run at 1.0. E3 goes on the one primary, E4 on fields, E6 is the top haze, E10 'landed' works on anchors, and E20 keeps the lamps breathing. Reduced motion and more contrast behave as the kit gives them.

3. 'Here' is the latch (T1-32), never the slab.
- Applies to .places a[aria-current], .tools a[aria-current], .menu.here>summary, .tabs a[aria-current], .kind-row[aria-current], .settings-nav a[aria-current], the phone tab bar and today's date on the month.
- Background color-mix(in srgb, var(--here) 24%, var(--bg)) (about #1c2328), an inset 2px top cap in --here-cap #a9c4d8, the label in --heading 600 and the icon in --here-cap.
- Check that it still wins the squint in the bar.

4. Links.
- Head links ('All plans', 'All 4', 'All the setup steps', 'All 12', 'Change a key', 'Change the limit'; selectors .section-head > a, .section-links a) are set in --ink-2 with a 1px underline in color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent), offset 4px, plus the arrow icon.
- On hover they turn --heading with a #9fb4d6 underline.
- Prose links keep #9fb4d6 underlined. Row titles stay ink, underlined on hover or focus.

5. Type on a 24px line.
- Title: 600 3rem/48px Plex Sans Condensed.
- Home's question: 600 3.25rem/1.05, the largest head on Home.
- Head: 1.75rem/32px. Lede: 1.125rem/28px. Body: 1rem/24px. Small: .9375rem/24px.
- A new --t-label, 600 .8125rem/20px Plex Sans, sentence case, no tracking. It replaces every uppercase --t-legend: table.month th (Mon to Sun), .eyebrow ('Who answers', 'What a lamp says', 'Parts'), 'No date', and the tally and key words.
- Mono only for dates, times, counts and money, always tabular.
- Words inside drawings: 12-13px Plex Mono, sentence case, with NOW their only capitals.
- Rows are 48px, and plate paddings and gaps are multiples of 12px.
- Curly apostrophes in every template: The kids’ wishes, Maya’s.
- text-wrap: balance on heads, pretty on paragraphs.

6. Captions: 'Fig. n' (numbered per page, no decimals), then one sentence saying how to read the figure, in --t-small, ink-2.

7. Kinds: .kind is a .75rem square in the kind's colour followed by the kind's name in .875rem Plex Sans 500, sentence case, --ink-2 ('Activity', 'Something to eat'). The colour lives in the square only.

HOME (home.html)

The greeting (.plate.welcome):
- Square corners (border-radius 0) and grid columns minmax(0,1fr) var(--fig-w).
- The words stay first and at the left. The Next up tube (.next-fig .crt.next-up) moves to the right, so the title is read before the glass (interaction).
- Light the pool from under the tube: radial-gradient(70% 90% at 100% 100%, rgb(109 255 156/.13), transparent 62%), with the blueprint whisper at the top left.
- Move the ::before scanline mask to 100% 100%. Raise the scanlines to 3.5% white if they do not show at 100% (soul).
- Keep the portrait tube's radar and its VT323 at three strengths, but size it to the words: about 21rem tall, radar 10rem, so there is no band under the form.
- Order stays: speaker line, question (still the textarea's label), box, then the ways to start (44px, 8px apart).

Coming up and To do (the day plate):
- Grid columns var(--fig-w) minmax(0,1.15fr) minmax(0,1fr). Delete fig-axis and axis(), and with them the four-symbol legend.
- Coming up's rows span columns 1-2 as the rail:
  - column 1: 'Sun 4 Oct' (Plex Mono .875rem, weekday --dim), right-aligned, then a numbered stop ring 1-4 (the .stop style) on the line, then the leader;
  - column 2: title, dotted leader, time, relative. The row loses its own date column, which is now on the rail.
- Above row 1, a .now-rule: 'Now' lit on the rail with its lamp, and the lit line crossing Coming up just under its head.
- Coming up's head: 'Coming up', then '4 after Next up' (T1-42), then All plans.
- Caption under the rail: 'Fig. 1 Coming up by day; the lit line is now.'
- To do (column 3):
  - rows: a neutral tick, the title, then owner and due words on a second line;
  - late rows get a 3px --people inset left edge and amber 'was due 3 days ago' (T1-16);
  - drop the '#4' ids;
  - a .now-rule with its lamp crosses the column between the late rows and the rest;
  - head: 'To do', then '4 open · 2 late' (2 late in amber, a link to To do), then All 4.

Setup and wishes: keep the track and the run-in bold actions. The end stop reads 'Then you’re ready.' in --dim beside a hollow ring, not a caps pill. 'The kids’ wishes'.

Lately added: columns kind (9rem: swatch and word) | title | for | '#1', right-aligned, tabular, --faint. Use the same columns in both halves.

Phone:
- The rail folds into the rows: the date becomes the row's first line.
- The NOW rules stay.
- The 'Fig. 1 · 5 plans…' disclosure becomes one row of three 44px links: '4 more plans · 4 to do · 2 late'.
- The tube follows the ways to start, in landscape, as now.

Footer: the mark and the legal line in the figure column, the tagline in the words column, on one baseline.

TO DO (tasks.html)
- Keep the rail and NOW, now with the two-layer light.
- Late rows: a neutral tick box (remove .tick.late's amber frame), a 3px amber edge and 'Late · was due 3 days ago' in amber.
- '#4' moves after the title in .8125rem Plex Mono, --faint.
- 'Edit, complete or snooze' becomes 'Edit' (pencil icon and word, 44px) at the right of the first line.
- 'No active reminder' is set in --faint.
- Pointing at a row lights its rail dot.
- Fig. 1 (the tally): draw the next-due mark as a 2px lit outline round its own bar, never a floating box (system). Legend in sentence case. Caption: 'A square for each open task, by whose it is: late filled amber, the next due lit.'

PLANS, MONTH (plans_month.html, the harness's plans shot)
- The head plate spans.
- THE WEEK RAIL is built into the table so it cannot miss a row:
  - a first column, var(--fig-w) plus var(--gap) wide, on the drawing sheet, with no cell borders; its right edge is the plate hairline;
  - in each week a <th scope='row' class='week-mark'> holds the week's range '28 Sep – 4 Oct' (Plex Mono .8125rem; --faint before today);
  - then a stop on the rail: a hollow ring when nothing is on, or filled --draw-2 with '2 plans' beside it;
  - then two 10px squares for Saturday and Sunday: --draw-fill when that day holds a plan, open when it is free, so free weekends read at a glance.
- In today's week the stop is the lit lamp. The NOW line leaves it, crosses the hairline and runs along the top edge of today's week row to today's cell, ending at today's lamp. That is soul's own ask: 'the lit NOW line crossing the month grid on today's row'.
- Earlier days take a .past class: faint numerals, events at 70%.
- Today's cell takes the latch (tint and cap), not the slab.
- Caption under the rail: 'Fig. 1 The weeks on the rail: a filled stop holds plans, an open square is a free weekend day; the lit line is now.'
- The month name and Earlier/Later stay on the head row.
- Phone: the month-list of busy days on the rail, with the NOW rule between past and coming.

PLANS, LIST (plans.html)
- fig-axis becomes the rail, as on Home, with NOW lit at the top crossing the list.
- The marks sit at each row's first line, so a second line (place, notes, 'Move it', 'Cancel it') never misaligns them.
- Recently keeps a rail of hollow, dim stops and has no NOW.

CHAT (chat.html)
- The head spans. The sequence thumbnail goes, and with it the dark band.
- The thread becomes the diagram. <ol class='thread'> spans the figure column and the words (subgrid).
- A first <li class='lanes'> heads the lanes in the figure column:
  - her screen at x 28px: presence at 2.5rem, with E19 bloom, scanlines and one glyph fall, above 'Vera';
  - each family member who has spoken (up to three, gathered in a Jinja namespace in order of their first line) as their initial in a steel square at x 96, 164 and 232px.
- The lifelines are dotted --draw verticals drawn as the thread's background.
- Each said-line gets from-lN and to-lN classes; Vera answers the lane of the family line before her. The line draws its arrow in the figure column at the height of its said-by line: a 1.5px --draw-2 ::before and an arrowhead ::after, with its number (01, 02…) in Plex Mono 12px over it.
- The newest arrow and its number are the live mark: lit with the two-layer halo, plus an arrival afterglow on #latest (E10).
- Pointing at a line lights its arrow.
- Her words stay on the glass at the left and the family's on steel slips at the right. The day rule spans both columns.
- Phone: the lanes and numbers are hidden.

IDEAS (ideas.html)
- The radar tube, at the full kit, leads the head. On the phone it is 9rem and follows the filters.
- The kinds chart gets a visible label, 'Show one kind' (13px, semibold). Its rows are 44px links. 'Every kind' and the chosen kind take the latch.
- On the phone the chart re-lays as a wrapping row of 44px keys just above the list. They are the same links, so there is still one control for the filter.
- The list: #id (--faint) | kind | title | drive, right-aligned Plex Mono tabular ('27 min', '2 h 10 min'), split from its compass in Jinja, under a 'Drive, about' column head | way ('S', 'NW') in its own 2.5rem --dim column | for.

STATUS (status.html)
- The head spans: title, lede, needs attention, then the three readings as links ('3 of 4 / answering', '1 of 4 / key set', '$0.00 of $2.00 / spent today'). There is no figure in the head, so no band.
- The lamps plate is led by the wiring (Fig. 1, sticky, sized to its drawing), with 'What a lamp says' in sentence case under it. Pointing at a row lights its port and wire.
- The spend plate is led by the page's one green screen, the original's own spend tube (E12-E15) in the thin case:
  - crt('spend-tube'), var(--fig-w) wide and sized to its words;
  - '$0.00' in VT323 2.5rem, bright;
  - 'of $2.00 today' at 1.25rem;
  - the character bar '[#.........] 0%' at 1.35rem, the original's [####....];
  - 'about $0.04 a day' in dim;
  - the power light;
  - --phosphor re-lit amber from 75% of the limit and red past it (kit E12).
  - It is aria-hidden, because the words beside it say the same.

SETTINGS
- Overview: under the machine and its caption, the part that needs a look: its amber ring numeral 8, then 'Sign-in and security: still the installer’s password' as a 44px link. This fills the empty column.
- Sections: the machine is capped at 13rem tall. 'Parts' is a sentence-case label. The current part takes the latch and is lit in the drawing.

FORM
- Keep the anatomy, with the part being typed in lit.
- The caption becomes a sentence, and labels are sentence case.

KEEP FOR THE HARNESS
- The classes .idea-card, .next-up, #title, .field.wide, label.check and details.menu>summary.
- Every form's csrf and once tokens.
- No script, inline style or outside address.
- Arrivals start at opacity .05 or more.
- Late, next and today are worked out once, in one _ui.html macro, from the app clock.
briefs.avoids:

- 'Plans has no phosphor' (soul): the lit NOW line and today's lamp.

- 'Home's Fig. 1 needs a four-symbol legend, is hard to read, is 60px taller than its lists, and draws the next plan as a pale dot': it becomes a rail level with its rows, with no legend.

briefs.title:
Tell Vera what to *plan*.

Kept: it is the lineage's best so far. It scored 8.02, was first for style, interaction and the skeptic, and joint first for usability.

In the manual's imperative it says who hears the box and names the whole job in one verb, and the lit word is that job. It stays the textarea's <label>. It is set as Home's largest head (3.25rem Plex Sans Condensed 600) directly over the box, with 'plan' under E1's two-layer halo. Nothing else on Home's first screen lights that word. It fits one line on a 390px phone.

briefs.name: Gauged Manual
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-figure-refine's files. Keep its plate, drawing sheet, bone ink, blueprint companion, faces, lit pool and 0 small targets.

Graft four gems, each rebuilt in the manual's own 1.25px blueprint line, Plex type and slate sheet so that none reads pasted. Then take the lineage's fixes listed at the end.

G1. ROUND GAUGES (L044): the page's one live number on a round tube.
- Build it from the lineage's own rebuild: macro round_screen in tour/t1-b/variants/t1-figure-graft/templates/_ui.html (lines 161-236) and its .dial and .ring-* rules (sheet.css 1054-1129). That rebuild came from Dessau: rounds/r13/variants/r13-wild-3/templates/_ui.html round_screen (88-114) and sheet.css 1064, 1116, 1207-1240 and 2044-2051.
- Size: a 12.5rem round crt sunk into the slate sheet inside a blueprint instrument ring 8px outside the glass.
- Glass: E13 blur of .35px, E14 scanlines and curved falloff, E12 80px spill, a power lamp at the ring's foot, and E16 power-on from a line starting at opacity .05.

(a) The Plans head, on both the list and the month:
- The ring carries 28 day ticks for the next four weeks, with a tick lit at each plan day and the arc from NOW (at the top) to the next plan lit.
- The glass carries three lines only: 'Next in' (VT323 1.25rem, dim), '1' (VT323 4.5rem, bright; the days to the next plan, from rel_days() or read from weeks' entries on the month), and 'day' (1.25rem).
- It reads 'Today' when the plan is today, and 'Clear' over 'four weeks' when nothing is planned.
- No word on the glass is under 1.25rem. That is the lesson Live Figures' 14px VT323 taught.
- The caption carries the plan in words: 'Fig. 1 Next: Silver Falls hike, tomorrow at 10:00.'
- The head (title, lede, the latched List/Month tabs, the source note) sits beside it, as tall as the tube, so there is no band.

(b) The Status spend plate: the same tube as a gauge (the scale= form).
- The glass shows '$0.00' at 2.75rem, bright, over 'of $2.00' at 1.25rem.
- The ring is a scale from $0 to the limit, with the spent arc lit, the limit tick lit, and a dim --draw-2 ghost tick at the 30-day average.
- --phos is re-lit amber from 75% and red past the limit (kit E12).
- Caption: 'Fig. 2 Today against the limit; the pale tick is an average day.'

Nowhere else. Not on To do: late stays amber words and an amber edge, never an amber tube (skeptic). Not on Settings. Not on Home, where the greeting keeps its portrait Next up tube. Each page keeps one green screen.

G2. QUIET WEEKS FOLDED (L122).
- Port Pocket's look-ahead from rounds/r11/variants/r11-wild-1/templates/plans_month.html (lines 39-69: namespace quiet_from and next_quiet; CSS .week.quiet in sheet.css 1669-1671) into Lit Manual's month <table>.
- A run of weeks that holds no plan and not today becomes one <tr class='quiet'><td colspan='7'>. It reads '31 Aug – 27 Sep' in Plex Mono, tabular, --ink-2, then 'Nothing on.' in --dim, and is 3rem tall.
- At each end of that row, a draughtsman's break mark: a small 1.25px --draw zigzag, as an inline SVG path, as a drawing marks a length left out.
- Weeks with a plan or with today keep full rows, raised to 6.5rem so events breathe. Today's week never folds.
- The phone's month-list gets the same line.
- The shot then reads as one line for four empty weeks and one full week that holds everything, where it now shows a grid of empty cells.

G3. PENCIL-HATCHED KIND LEGEND (L022).
- Source: rounds/r13/variants/r13-wild-1/sheet.css .swatch and .legend (1353-1391), its per-kind --accent map (about 60-75), and palette rounds/r13/palettes/r13-wild-1.json. Its outing is moss #b0c98a, never a phosphor green.
- Define pencil inks per kind: --pencil: color-mix(in oklch, var(--kc) 78%, #8f948c). Check that the seven kinds stay at least 12 apart.
- (a) Every kind legend entry: .kind in Lately added, the Ideas list, the idea page and Restaurants. It is an 18px square (20px in Lately added) with a 1.25px pencil border, filled with repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, pencil 0 1.25px, transparent 1.25px 5px). Then the kind in .875rem Plex Sans 500, sentence case, --ink-2. This replaces the flat square and the 12px tracked caps.
- (b) Ideas' kinds chart, which is the Kind filter: each bar is drawn in the same hatching inside its pencil border, its length the count, with the count tabular at the right.
  - It is labelled 'Show one kind'.
  - 'Every kind' and the chosen kind take the 2px steel latch.
  - On the phone it becomes a wrapping row of 44px keys above the list.
- The kind colour becomes a drawn material, pencil on the drawing sheet, not a fill or a glow.

G4. DIMENSION LINES FROM NOW (L167).
- Source: rounds/r13/variants/r13-wild-1/sheet.css .rel with ::before and ::after (1053-1075) and templates/home.html (49-80).
- Every plan row's relative cell (.p-rel on Home's Coming up, and on the Plans list's Coming up and Recently) is set as a dimension:
  - a fixed 8.5rem cell;
  - the words centred in .9375rem Plex Sans, sentence case, tabular figures ('in 4 days', 'in 2 weeks', 'tomorrow');
  - on each side a 1px centre line in --draw at 65%, ending in a 10px end tick.
- The ends stay low-contrast and there are no caps, per the entry's caveat, so it never reads as brackets.
- A plan today reads 'today' with lit ticks, the only lit dimension. Past plans are dim ('3 days ago').

THE LINEAGE'S FIXES, taken as the refinement names them:
- 'Here' is a tint plus a 2px --here-cap latch (T1-32), never the slab.
- Head links are --ink-2 with a 1px blueprint underline and an arrow.
- Home's day plate: the axis becomes the rail.
  - Plans only, each date level with its Coming up row, stops numbered 1-4 as the rows are, and NOW lit crossing Coming up. There is no legend.
  - The G4 dimensions sit in those rows.
  - A NOW rule crosses Home's To do between late and due.
- Late rows: a neutral tick with a 3px amber edge (T1-16), and '#4' after the title in --faint.
- 'Edit' instead of 'Edit, complete or snooze'.
- The tally's next-due is a lit outline on its bar.
- READY becomes plain words.
- On the phone, the Fig. 1 disclosure becomes three 44px links ('4 more plans · 4 to do · 2 late').
- Status's head spans with its three readings, and the wiring leads the lamps plate.
- The Settings overview column is filled with the needs-a-look link.
- Every lit mark gets the kit's two layers. Pointing at a row lights its mark over 0.12s and 1.2s.
- 13px sentence-case eyebrows and column heads, curly apostrophes, a 24px line.

WHERE IT DIFFERS FROM THE REFINEMENT, on purpose, so the judges can compare:
- The greeting keeps its tube at the LEFT, so the figure-left rule holds on every plate. The tube is sized to the words' height, the pool is squared, and the question is 3.25rem so the title still wins the squint.
- Chat: the sequence thumbnail folds into the transcript's own hung numbers. Each number (01, 02…) gets a small blueprint arrow: → for a line to Vera, ← for hers. The newest is lit with afterglow. The Chat plate spans with no figure column, and her screen on her lines keeps E19's bloom.
- The Plans month keeps a full-width table. Its figure is the G1 tube in the head, and today takes the latch and its lamp.

KEEP FOR THE HARNESS
- .idea-card, .next-up, #title, .field.wide, label.check and details.menu>summary.
- Every csrf and once token.
- No script, inline style or outside address.
- Arrivals start at opacity .05 or more.
- The glass is aria-hidden, and its words are also said in the captions and rows.

- 'The chat's sequence figure misses its lines and adds nothing': folded into the hung numbers.

It avoids Live Figures' own failures:
- VT323 too small in the rings: every word on the glass is 1.25rem or more.
- Amber '2 LATE' read as a warning costume: no tube on To do.
- Filler figures and round tubes on every page: tubes on Plans and Status only.
- Numbered tabs: none.
- The lit pool lost: kept.

It avoids each gem's caveats:
- L022 'loudest colour at 36px': 18-20px swatches with lowered chroma.
- L167 'reads as brackets, condensed caps': low-contrast ends, sentence case.
- L122 'today's week must never fold'.
- L044 'must show a figure the page does not already print': days to the next plan, spend against the limit.

It avoids convergence: no departures board, no meridian chat, no Desk Terminal column, no Pocket spine or month-on-a-pocket-tube. Every device is set in the manual's own line.
briefs.title:
*Plan* it with Vera.

New and untried. It keeps the manual's imperative (an operator's step) and answers the two faults the judges found in 'Tell Vera what to plan.':
- It no longer reads as if Vera does the planning. The family plans with her.
- 'It' takes whatever the family brings, whether a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder or the calendar, so the title is no narrower than the job. The placeholder under it then answers what 'it' can be.

The lit word opens the line and is the job itself, in E1's two layers. At 18 characters it holds one line on a 390px phone at 3rem. It stays the textarea's <label>, and no other glow on Home claims the word.
